### The analogs say the multiple, not the business, decides

| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft | cautionary | 1999-2012 | Free cash flow per share tripled from $1.15 to $3.45 while the share price fell 54% from $58.38 to $26.71 and $100 became $51 with dividends reinvested; the P/FCF multiple went from 51x to 8x | S154 |
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2025 | The split-adjusted record of $80.06 set on 2000-03-27 was not exceeded until 2025-12-10, a 25-year round trip, while revenue kept growing | S155 |
| Apple | cautionary | 2005-2014 | Apple's own P/E fell from 45.25x to 12.46x while earnings grew, so a low-teens multiple is in this company's history | S156 |

No best-case analog is close enough to carry the bull case, and that absence is a finding: no mega-cap franchise in the register has re-rated upward from 40x without an acceleration in reported growth. The three cautionary cases teach a decision rule rather than a forecast: when the entry multiple is the main contributor to expected return, growth has to be demonstrated before the multiple is paid. Apple at 40.0x on 8.1% consensus EPS growth is a milder version of the same configuration — 37.3x price-to-free-cash-flow against Microsoft's 51x — but the mechanism is identical, and half of Apple's last five years of return came from the multiple rather than from earnings [S154, S155].

The strongest counter-case is that the quality deserves the multiple. Apple's trailing free cash flow of $136,683M is 1.71 times Microsoft and Alphabet combined, its 2.68% cash yield grows at 8% a year, and at an 8.0% required return the reverse DCF needs only 5.7% perpetual growth, which the 8.9% five-year free-cash-flow compound has already cleared. A long-only fund that owns the S&P 500 already holds 7.25% Apple through the index, so the active decision is whether to hold more than the benchmark; at 36.5x forward earnings the answer is no until the price or the growth changes [S97, S93].

### The price at which the case turns

The case turns at a price. Risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $9.10 is the base and bear cases weighted 60/40 — 0.60 × $9.56 + 0.40 × $8.42, where $8.42 is the bear's $8.60 less the $0.18 of FY2027 amortisation on the FY2026 intangible additions; the bull is excluded because it needs unit evidence the filings do not yet show. At 30-33x that gives an entry band of $273-$300, and the top is the probability-weighted value itself, so nothing above $300 should be bought. The decision tree: watch at zero position until the FY2026 fourth-quarter print on 2026-11-02 and the December quarter; buy a starter at or below $300 if gross margin holds at 48% or better excluding refunds with double-digit Services growth; pass if memory takes gross margin below 47% or a final remedy removes commission. Confidence is high that the current price has no margin of safety and medium on the level of fair value, because the WACC moves the discounted value from $132 to $198. Open diligence: does the FY2026 10-K disclose intangible lives and the licensing counterparty, and does the December quarter hold 48% gross margin ex-refund? The fastest falsifier is evidence that the AI cycle is producing units rather than features [S7].

## 退出策略分析 Exit Strategy Analysis

Half of Apple's 134% five-year price gain came from its multiple rising from 26.6x to 40.0x, and with the probability-weighted outcome at $300 — 14.0% below the $348.91 close — the discipline for a long-only holder is a trim rule tied to the multiple, not an exit on news. The decomposition closes exactly: from the $148.96 close on 2021-11-01 to $348.91 on 2026-10-29 the shares returned 134.2%, diluted EPS moved from $5.61 to $8.72 (+55.4%, 9.2% a year), the P/E paid for those earnings moved from 26.6x to 40.0x (+50.7%) and dividends added 3.3% cumulatively; multiple expansion is 48% of the logarithmic return [S5, S6, S7].

| Component | 2021-11-01 to 2026-10-29 | Annualised | Share of return | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Share price | $148.96 → $348.91, +134.2% | +18.5% | — | S7 |
| Diluted EPS | $5.61 (FY2021) → $8.72 (TTM) | +9.2% | 50% | S6 |
| P/E multiple | 26.6x → 40.0x, +50.7% | +8.5% | 48% | S6, S7 |
| Dividends per share | $0.90 → $1.07, 3.3% cumulative | 0.65% | 2% | S6, S93 |

That history is the base rate a buyer is fighting. Apple's own filing puts $100 invested in September 2020 at $234 five years later, against $217 for the S&P 500 and $287 for the Dow Jones U.S. Technology index — 18.5% a year against 16.8% and 23.5%, so the quality compounder beat the index by 8% cumulatively and lagged its own sector by 24%. Run forward, the same decomposition produces the expected return: on the 20/40/40 split the weighted exit multiple is 32.0x FY2027E earnings against the 36.5x paid today (−12.3 points) and the weighted EPS is 2.9% below consensus because the bear's $8.60 carries 40% weight (−2.9 points), with the interaction taking the total to −14.0%. The bull case's 8.4% annual return at a held 40x — 8.1% EPS growth, of which 1.6 points is buyback, plus a 0.31% dividend — is a 20% branch, not the base case [S5, S93].

| Route | Named buyer or venue | Rationale | Timing | Likelihood | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sale in the market | NasdaqGS, any investor | $13.22B traded a day; a $250M position is 1.9% of one day's value | Any session | Certain | S7 |
| Indirect exit through buyback | Apple Inc. itself | $82.2B trailing repurchases equal 1.6% of shares; $99.779B authorised at 2025-09-27, with $62.1B used in nine months leaving $37.7B | Renewed each May | High, but capped at 1.6% of shares a year | S5, S6 |
| Dividend | Apple Inc. | $0.27 a quarter, $1.08 annualised, 0.31% yield | Quarterly | Certain, immaterial alone | S47 |
| Index and passive flows | S&P 500 trackers | Apple is one of three stocks that make up 21% of the index | Continuous | Certain, and it works both ways | S97 |
| Strategic acquisition | None identified | The largest technology deal ever, $68.7B, is 1.35% of Apple's $5,029.9B enterprise value | None | 0% | S91, S98 |
| Take-private or break-up | No sponsor; no activist campaign disclosed | More than $5T of equity would be required | None | 0% | S6 |

Every incremental dollar of return has to come from the market, and the market will pay whatever multiple prevails when the holder sells; there is no bid to negotiate, no premium to extract and no lock-up to wait out. Liquidity is not the constraint — 38.67M shares and $13.22B change hands daily, so a $250M position is 1.9% of one day's value — but index concentration cuts the other way: Apple is one of three stocks making up 21% of the S&P 500, so passive flows amplify both directions, and the 52-week range of $243.42 to $351.73 is a 44.5% spread in a year in which the business did nothing but improve [S7, S97].

| Transaction | Year | Value | Multiple | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft / Activision Blizzard | 2022 announced, 2023 closed | $68.7B all cash | Not disclosed in the sources retrieved | S91 |
| Dell / EMC | 2016 | $67B | Not disclosed in the sources retrieved | S98 |
| Broadcom / VMware | 2023 | $61B | Not disclosed in the sources retrieved | S98 |
| Apple buyback, May 2025 programme | 2025 | $100B authorisation | 1.6% of shares a year on $82.2B trailing spend | S5, S6 |

The precedent set is deliberately unhelpful, and that is the finding: no transaction multiple anchors this exit because no deal of comparable size exists, and the three largest technology transactions ever are each 1.2-1.4% of Apple's enterprise value. What the precedents establish is the ceiling — an acquirer able to write a $5T cheque would face antitrust review in every major jurisdiction before financing, and the DOJ's monopolisation case filed on 2024-03-21 shows how the company's scale is treated [S91, S98, S5].

The dated catalysts are what a holder trades around. Full-year FY2026 results arrive on 2026-11-02, the first call chaired by John Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook as CEO on 2026-09-01; the September-quarter print follows in late January 2027, since FQ1 FY2026 was released on 2026-01-29; the next buyback authorisation should accompany FQ2 results in May 2027, following the $110B of May 2024 and $100B of May 2025; and the regulatory file runs in parallel — the EU's DMA Article 6(4) investigation can end in fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales, and the search-default remedies that let Google keep paying Apple are on non-exclusive, twelve-month terms now under appeal at the D.C. Circuit. The Google payment is the highest-margin revenue Apple receives and is not separately disclosed, so its renewal is a Services-margin event rather than a headline risk [S92, S54, S5, S99].

| Scenario | Exit multiple × FY2027E EPS | Price | Return from $348.91 | Weight | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull: AI cycle extends, multiple holds | 40x × $10.10 | $404 | +15.8% | 20% | S93, S6 |
| Base: multiple drifts to FY2025 level | 34x × $9.56 | $325 | −6.9% | 40% | S93, S6 |
| Bear: margin reversal, multiple to FY2023 | 26x × $8.60 | $224 | −35.8% | 40% | S93, S6 |
| Probability-weighted | — | $300 | −14.0% before the 0.31% dividend | 100% | S6, S93, model |

The scenario table is where entry price does all the work, and the sensitivity runs on the same three multiples rather than a fourth set: holding two years to FY2028 EPS of $10.32, an exit at 40x returns +18.9% including dividends, at 34x +1.2% and at 26x −22.5% — a 41.4-point spread produced entirely by fourteen points of multiple, with the 26x branch carrying 40% weight. The downside is not hypothetical: the shares traded at $243.42 within the past year, 30.2% below today's close, and the five-year closing low of $125.02 is 64.2% below it. The strongest counter-evidence to a trim is that this re-rating has punished patience — a holder who trimmed at 37.5x in fiscal 2024 missed the following 50% — and that 1.6% share shrinkage plus 8.1% EPS growth plus the dividend is an 8-10% annual return with no re-rating at all, an acceptable long-only outcome. For a watchlist the discipline follows: size for a 30% drawdown rather than treating the 44.5% range as unusual, because at 40x it is not; trim into strength above 40x forward earnings, $382 on FY2027E EPS of $9.56; and add only at $273-$300 — 30-34x the $9.10 blended FY2027 EPS ($9.56 base, $8.42 bear), capped at the $300 expected value because 34x on $9.10 is $309. Neither condition exists at $348.91, so the position is zero, revisited after the 2026-11-02 print and the May 2027 buyback authorisation [S5, S7, S93].

## ESG评估 ESG Assessment

Apple's ESG exposure is a platform-regulation problem, not a carbon or governance one: seven jurisdictions target the 75.4%-gross-margin Services pool — $109.2bn of FY2025 sales and $82.3bn of gross profit, 42.2% of the total — while fines to date (€500m EU, €150m France, $15.5m Korea) are less than 0.2% of $416.2bn of net sales and the remedies can permanently lower the highest-margin revenue Apple has. [S5, S134, S137, S136]

### The EU has established the principle; the size is still open

On 2025-04-23 the European Commission fined Apple €500m for breaching the DMA's anti-steering obligation and ordered the restrictions removed within 60 days; a separate Article 6(4) case on developer contract terms, opened 2024-06-24, remains unresolved with a statutory ceiling of 10% of worldwide net sales ($41.6bn). The fine is a rounding error, but the principle is durable: the General Court rejected Apple's challenge to its gatekeeper designation on 2026-07-08. The cash question is the EU link-out commission. [S6, S134, S135]

### The US is the largest and slowest remedy risk

The DOJ and 15 states plus DC sued Apple for monopolization on 2024-03-21 in New Jersey seeking equitable relief; the motion to dismiss failed and by July 2026 the parties were in early settlement talks, with discovery to late May 2027 and no trial date. In Epic v. Apple the district court found contempt on 2025-04-30 and barred fees on out-of-app purchases; the Ninth Circuit on 2025-12-11 allowed some link-out commission and the Supreme Court agreed to review the contempt standard on 2026-06-30. Google search remedies finalised in December 2025 also threaten distribution payments inside Services, of undisclosed size. [S6, S62, S138]

### Enforcement is fragmenting; privacy is now an antitrust issue

The UK CMA designated Apple with strategic market status on 2025-10-22 and by 2026-10-20 was consulting on steering and NFC conduct requirements. Korea's communications regulator fined Apple KRW 20.81bn ($15.5m) on 2026-10-28 and ordered payment links and revised commissions, ruling a 26% fee on third-party billing evaded the 30% norm. Japan's Mobile Software Competition Act took effect on 2025-12-18, and 48 Chinese developers complained to SAMR on 2026-06-23. France's competition authority fined Apple €150m on 2025-03-31 over App Tracking Transparency, treating a privacy feature as abuse of dominance. The pattern is convergence of the global take rate toward the mid-teens, not one catastrophic penalty. [S132, S136, S140, S139, S141, S137]

### Environmental, labour and governance risks are not the discount drivers

Apple's 2025 emissions were more than 60% below 2015 and flat versus 2024, against a 2030 target of a 75% cut before carbon removals balance the remainder; removal volumes and costs are undisclosed, so the claim is only partially verified. Manufacturing remains concentrated in China, India and Vietnam, and the 10-K flags supplier industrial-accident risk; India's production-linked incentive has shifted capacity — cumulative iPhone exports passed $50bn by December 2025 and reached ₹2 lakh crore in FY2026 — but this is subsidy-supported diversification, not a structural cost advantage. Governance is cleaner than the sector: one share class, an independent chair in Art Levinson and eight directors; the 2026 proxy discloses no material related-party transactions beyond a former operating chief's family member earning above $120,000, and Tim Cook's 2025 target pay was $59m with 92% support on the 2025 say-on-pay vote. The live issues are succession (Cook is 65) and political exposure: shareholders rejected a "China Entanglement Audit" proposal on 2026-02-24. There is no dual-class discount. [S144, S145, S146, S143, S5, S52, S100]

### Policy is two different risks: sunk tax and reversible trade

The policy matrix separates sunk tax from reversible trade. State Aid is finished cash — the ECJ confirmed the Commission's 2016 decision on 2024-09-10 — a precedent risk, not an open liability. Tariffs are the opposite: the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and Apple is claiming refunds, the Section 232 semiconductor review imposed no tariffs on Apple's products on 2026-01-14, but Section 301 actions remain live. Price trade policy as gross-margin volatility, not permanent impairment. [S6]

### What the investor should price

Separate the fine from the remedy. Fines to date are immaterial, and even a maximum DMA fine would be a single charge. The durable exposure is the commission pool: the matrix shows what a cut in Services gross profit would do to operating income. That argues for a haircut to Services earnings, not for avoiding the stock. Confidence is medium because Apple does not disclose App Store revenue or take rates, and the DOJ and EU timetables have slipped repeatedly.

### Diligence questions

Five questions would change the assessment: what share of Services revenue and gross profit is App Store commission revenue by region; what commission Apple collects on US and EU link-outs; whether Article 6(4) brings periodic penalties or structural separation; the annual value of Google search-distribution payments; and the contracted volume and cost of carbon removals behind Apple 2030. The first two sit outside the public filing set; a PACER data request has been filed. If App Store commission revenue is below a tenth of Services gross profit, regulation is a sentiment issue; if a quarter or more, an earnings issue.

## 综合评分与投资建议 Comprehensive Scoring & Recommendation

Apple scores 5.7 out of 10, and the score is a verdict on price rather than on quality. The business earns a 9 and the ecosystem an 8, but valuation earns a 2 and regulatory exposure a 4, and those two dimensions carry 30% of the weight against a 36.5x forward multiple that the market has already paid. The composite is the weighted average of the table below; quality justifies a premium multiple, not the size of the premium the shares now carry [S93].

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and unit economics | 15% | 9 | Nine-month FY2026 revenue of $364,357M at a 49.1% gross margin, with $136,683M of trailing free cash flow at 1.06x net income on capex of 2.2% of sales | S6, S47 |
| Competitive moat and ecosystem | 15% | 8 | More than 2.5bn active devices and 65% of the $600-plus tier; the assistant layer is licensed from Google, so the intelligence moat is rented | S6, S115 |
| Market growth | 10% | 5 | Shipments fall 16.7% while ASPs rise 27.6%, so growth is price and mix; FY2027 consensus EPS growth decelerates to 8.1% | S79, S93 |
| Margin durability and pricing power | 10% | 6 | Memory costs may materially hurt gross margin; mobile DRAM contract prices rose 78-83% quarter on quarter for LPDDR5X in Q2 2026, and 2 points of the June-quarter margin were tariff refunds | S6, S148 |
| Management and capital allocation | 10% | 6 | $82,226M of trailing buybacks at 40.0x earnings give a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.99% Treasury; the CEO, COO, CFO and general counsel all changed within twenty months | S6, S47 |
| Earnings quality and balance sheet | 5% | 8 | Free cash flow converts at 1.06x net income with net cash of $62,173M, but $13,270M of gross intangibles were added in nine months and $5,075M is already current | S6, S47 |
| Regulatory and policy risk | 10% | 4 | The Google payment is reported at $20bn a year, 12.9% of trailing operating income; the EU Article 6(4) case carries a 10%-of-sales cap with terms live since 2026-10-01 | S147, S134 |
| Valuation and margin of safety | 20% | 2 | 40.0x trailing, 32.5x EV/EBIT and 36.5x FY2027E against an 18.1x peer median and an 18.59x S&P 500 forward multiple on 2026-10-29; the DCF returns $158 | S7, S93, S153 |
| Catalysts and exit path | 5% | 5 | The 2026-11-02 print and the May 2027 buyback authorisation are dated, but the largest technology deal ever is 1.35% of enterprise value | S92, S91 |
| Composite | 100% | 5.7 | Weighted average of the nine dimensions | S6, S93 |

The quality scores are not in dispute. A franchise that converts a quarter of its revenue into gross profit and funds its buybacks from operations rather than from the balance sheet deserves a premium to the market, and the four-peer median is pulled down by a memory maker whose earnings multiple is lowest exactly when its earnings peak. But the premium now paid is at a cyclical high in gross margin and at the top of a five-year re-rating, so the table separates the franchise, which is the strongest in mega-cap technology, from the entry price, which is not.

### The recommendation and what changes it

The rating is Watchlist with a zero position, a 12-24 month horizon and medium evidence confidence. It changes in three directions. Downside: the bear case already carries a 40% weight at $224 (-35.8%); at 26x on bear EPS of $8.00 the value is $208 (-40%), and a final EU structural remedy that removes commission makes the bear the base at $270. Upside: a ten-year yield below 4% would lower the discount rate, move the rating to Hold and raise the valuation score to 4. Operating: a December-2026 quarter with gross margin at 48% or better excluding refunds and Services growth in double digits would justify a starter position inside the band. The band is $273-$300: $9.10 of risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS — the base and bear cases weighted 60/40, with the bull excluded until units appear — at 30-33x, capped at the $300 probability-weighted value so that no purchase inside it is negative-expectation [S7, S10].

### Position sizing and the regime

Position sizing is where the negative expected return becomes an instruction. The Kelly fraction, with its inputs in the table below, is negative because the probability-weighted outcome sits below the current price, so the optimal bet is zero. A long-only fund that wants the name would cap it at the weight in the table once the entry conditions are met, because the downside is a multiple event rather than a solvency event: net cash and the services annuity survive every stress in the risk matrix.

The regime supports patience rather than exposure. The index is near a record with volatility mid-range and credit spreads tight, yet technology is being rotated out and the ten-year yield stands near its cycle high, so a cash yield well below it has no valuation cushion. In a rotation-out regime with open EU and DOJ cases, the appropriate approach is to discount the target multiple rather than to pay it.

### Next diligence and the conditions to invest

Three actions come before any purchase. First, read the FY2026 10-K due with the 2026-11-02 results for the intangible note — lives, counterparty and the $5,075M current portion that implies $0.16 of FY2027 amortisation — and for the fourth-quarter buyback pace. Second, wait for the December-2026 quarter and test two numbers: gross margin at 48% or better excluding tariff refunds, and Services growth at 10% or more with the EU's post-October commission card in force. Third, ask Apple investor relations, and if necessary the court record, for the share of Services revenue from App Store commission and from the Google default payment. The conditions for a starter position are a price at or below $300, a gross margin print at or above 48% excluding refunds, and double-digit Services growth; the conditions to pass are a gross margin below 47% like-for-like or a final remedy that removes commission [S6, S147].

1. Apple earns a composite of 5.7: a 9 for business quality and an 8 for its moat are outweighed by a 2 for valuation at 40.0x trailing earnings against an 18.1x peer median, so the watchlist rating is a price judgement rather than a quality one [S93].
2. The position is zero at $348.91: the Kelly fraction is -1.62 on a 20/40/40 distribution whose probability-weighted value is $300 (-14.0%), and the maximum loss to the bear case is -35.8% [S6].
3. Buy only inside $273-$300 — 30-33x $9.10, the 60/40 base-bear EPS — and only after the December-2026 quarter shows gross margin at 48% or better excluding tariff refunds with Services growth in double digits [S7].
